newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota fieldwork improves, carcasses buried.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota fieldwork improves, carcasses buried.

text.p: Favorable weather in the week ended on May 4 aided fieldwork and flood cleanup in North Dakota, the state's agricultural statistics service said.
The statewide starting date for fieldwork was May 3, well behind the 5-year average of April 22. Planting remains well behind averages but only slightly behind last year.
Removal of livestock carcasses from waterways following the recent flooding continued. As of May 4, 840 carcasses had been removed from water and 12,174 carcasses buried statewide.
Carcass removal and burial should be completed in the western two thirds of the state by this week, it said.
Spring wheat seeded 3 pct vs nil week ago, 4 year ago, 25 on a five-year average.
Durum seeded 3 pct vs 1 w/a, 2 y/a, 13 avge.
Barley seeded 2 pct vs 0 w/a, 4 y/a, 25 avge.
Oats seeded 1 pct vs 0 w/a, 4 y/a, 25 avge.
Sugarbeet seeded 23 pct vs 3 w/a, 5 y/a, 38 avge.
Corn seeded 5 pct vs nil, 3 y/a, 7 avge.
Average soil temperatures on May 4 ranged from a low of 43 degrees Fahrenheit at Langdon in the northeast to 58 degrees F in Linton in the south central part of the state.

The agency said 77 percent of cattle and 75 percent of sheep were on supplemental feeding. Supplies of hay and roughage were rated 61 percent adequate to surplus and supply of grain and concentrates rated 81 percent adequate to surplus, both unchanged to higher than last week.
